dimensions.assessment: Affects only individual Members of Congress who face expulsion or specific ethics violations resulting in a Statement of Alleged Violation upon resignation.
dimensions.evidence: If an individual is expelled from Congress, all Member service previously performed by such individual shall be noncreditable

dimensions.assessment: Results in the complete forfeiture of federal pension eligibility and government TSP contributions for the affected individuals, though impact is limited to a small number of persons.
dimensions.evidence: all contributions made by the Government for the benefit of that individual... and all earnings attributable to such contributions, shall be forfeited.

dimensions.assessment: Federal budgetary effects are negligible, involving only the return of lump-sum personal contributions and forfeiture of specific government retirement contributions for a handful of lawmakers.
dimensions.evidence: that portion of such individual's lump-sum credit which is attributable to such Member service... shall, on proper application, be payable to such individual

dimensions.assessment: Amends Title 5 of the United States Code regarding federal civil service and retirement systems (CSRS and FERS) for congressional members.
dimensions.evidence: Subchapter III of chapter 83 of title 5, United States Code, is amended by inserting after section 8333 the following

dimensions.assessment: Establishes a permanent statutory rule applicable to future Congresses for acts committed after the date of enactment.
dimensions.evidence: The amendments made by this Act shall apply with respect to any expulsion or any Statement of Alleged Violation... based... on any act committed... after the date of the enactment of this Act.

missing_information: Historical data on the exact number of future members who might trigger these provisions.
importance_detail.rationale: The Congressional Pension Accountability Act applies narrowly to individual Members of Congress who are expelled or resign following specific ethics violations, rendering their past Member service noncreditable for federal retirement annuities.
